faq.q: Which essay types does it structure?
faq.a: Nine: argumentative, expository, narrative, descriptive, compare & contrast, cause & effect, problem-solution, UPSC analytical essay, and school exam essay. Each produces a different skeleton — the argumentative type, for example, includes a dedicated counter-argument and rebuttal section, while the UPSC type uses a quote-anchored intro, multi-dimensional body (social, political, economic, ethical angles), way forward and optimistic conclusion.

faq.q: How are the word counts per section decided?
faq.a: You enter a total word count (default 1000) and number of body paragraphs (1–8), and it distributes the words across sections by weight — the introduction and conclusion get a smaller share, body and counter-argument sections more — then rounds them to sum exactly to your total. Each section header shows its word budget so you can plan pacing before writing.

faq.q: Can I edit the generated outline?
faq.a: Yes. You can reorder sections up/down, rename them, delete them (keeping at least one), add new sections, and type your own notes under each — the notes and structure are saved in your browser (essayOutline) and restored next visit. The section points are prompts (topic sentence, evidence slot, analysis, transition) you fill in yourself; the tool supplies no facts.

faq.q: Is there help with openings and transitions?
faq.a: Yes — an Insert Bank offers hook types (rhetorical question, startling statistic, quotation, anecdote, etc.), transition phrases, and conclusion techniques; click any to copy it. The UPSC type additionally shows guidance on structure, quoting sparingly, balance, and a ~10 min plan / 50 min write / 5 min review time split. Export the outline as copy, .txt or print/PDF.
